device_analysis.topology_reasoning: The image shows three parallel waveguides arranged vertically. The top and bottom guides have smooth taper transitions on the right side. The center guide is shorter and offset. This is a classic directional coupler architecture where the center waveguide acts as a coupling bus or middle port, and the top/bottom are input/output ports.
function_defining_knobs: wg_width: base waveguide width in μm
wg_spacing: center-to-center spacing between waveguides in μm
left_section_length: length of left straight section before taper in μm
taper_length: length of the taper region in μm
taper_tip_width: width at the narrow end of the taper in μm
center_wg_offset: horizontal offset of center waveguide from left edge in μm
center_wg_length: actual length of center waveguide in μm

iterations.notes: Initial baseline: straight sections + linear tapers. Limited by the inability to generate smooth S-curves with primitives alone.

final_summary.reason: IoU plateaued at ~0.18-0.19 after systematic parameter sweeps. Target geometry requires smooth S-curve tapers which cannot be accurately approximated with linear gdsfactory primitives (straight + linear taper). A full inverse-synthesis solution would require curve-fitting or Bezier path extrusion.

knob_verification.response_expected: Linear increase in layer area with width delta
knob_verification.status: Not formally tested due to device structure (coupler, not MZI) - spec_optimization.verify_knob_response expects delta_length.json. Manual verification confirms wg_width changes layer area as expected.
